inspectionPrice.note: BAR does not regulate inspection prices. It publishes monthly averages that stations self-report.
inspectionPrice.certificateFeeDetail: 'The station must charge a $8.25 Smog Check certificate fee.' 'Inspection prices are not regulated by BAR.'
inspectionPrice.certificateOnlyOnPass: Secondary sites (smogcheck.com blog) say the $8.25 is charged only when the vehicle passes. BAR's page wasn't read as saying so.

rules: Gasoline, hybrid and alternative-fuel vehicles of model year 1976 and newer, and diesels of model year 1998 and newer, are subject to Smog Check.
Gasoline, hybrid and alternative-fuel vehicles eight model years old or newer do not need a Smog Check at registration renewal; they pay a smog abatement fee instead.
Vehicles four model years old or newer are exempt from the change-of-ownership Smog Check (DMV charges an $8 smog transfer fee instead).
Change of ownership: a private seller must supply a passing certificate (valid 90 days); for dealers it is valid for two years.
Biennial: renewal requires a Smog Check every other year once the vehicle is past the eight-model-year exemption, in the biennial (smog-required) areas; 33 counties are listed by DMV.
Exempt: electric vehicles, motorcycles, gasoline vehicles 1975 and older, and diesels 1997 and older or over 14,000 lbs.
whoNeedsOne.publisher: California Bureau of Automotive Repair; California DMV

smogAbatementFee.correction: The $25 fee does not apply to all of a car's first eight years. Under AB 1274 (effective January 1, 2019) the $25 annual fee applies only to vehicles that are seven and eight model years old. Vehicles six model years old or less pay the older $20 annual fee. The fee is due only at registration renewal, and only in a biennial smog area.
smogAbatementFee.detail: The DMV bulletin: 'Requires an annual $25 smog abatement fee for vehicles that are seven and eight model years old' and 'the current annual $20 smog abatement fee for vehicles that are six or less model years old remains in effect.' The current DMV fees page lists 'Smog abatement (HSC §44060(d)(1)) $20' and 'Smog transfer (VC §4000.1) $8'.
smogAbatementFee.publisher: California DMV (Vehicle Industry News VIN 2018-19; Registration Fees page)
smogAbatementFee.date: Bulletin effective 2019-01-01, distributed October 2018; fees page accessed 2026-09-30

failRate.note: OIS is the OBD-based test for 2000-and-newer vehicles, and BAR-97 is the tailpipe test for older ones. Most cars a player would own take OIS, at about 7.5%.

modifiedSoftware.rule: Cal. Code Regs. tit. 16 §3340.42.2(c)(8), adopted 2013-07-01: fail if 'The vehicle's OBD system data does not match the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) or an Air Resources Board (ARB) exempted OBD software configuration.' Vehicle Code §27156 bars tampering, and software counts as part of the emissions control system.
modifiedSoftware.outcome: The vehicle fails, and the inspection report reads 'Modified Software'. It counts as a 'tampered' result, which excludes the vehicle from BAR's Repair Assistance Program until corrected. Software approved by a CARB Executive Order is allowed.
modifiedSoftware.fix: 'The vehicle's software must be restored to an OEM version or a CARB EO approved version.' The owner has a licensed repair facility restore the OEM software, then retests at any licensed Smog Check station, except that vehicles first directed to a STAR or Referee station must return to that station type.
modifiedSoftware.expectedVolume: BAR's preliminary analysis in 2021 put it at 5 to 10 vehicles failing per day statewide for Modified Software.
modifiedSoftware.costNote: No published price was found. The August 2026 BAR report doesn't break out Modified Software failures. Forum claims (for example '$100' to send an ECU back to the tuner) aren't usable.
modifiedSoftware.publisher: California Bureau of Automotive Repair (Paul Hedglin, Engineering and Research Branch, BAR Advisory Group meeting)

referee.what: The Smog Check Referee Program is BAR's dispute and special-case service, located at community colleges. It reviews contested Smog Check results; inspects unusual vehicles (kit cars, specially constructed vehicles, engine changes, modified vehicles); resolves emissions-related and exhaust-noise citations; locates hard-to-find emissions parts; and handles repair cost waivers and smog exemptions. If the owner of a car that failed for Modified Software insists the software is OEM, the Referee requires signed documentation from an OEM dealer stating that the software version, Cal ID and CVN are correct for that exact vehicle.
referee.fees: The Referee's exhaust-noise inspection certificate is $108 (asktheref.org FAQ). General services were described as free ('There are no fees for services') only in a search summary, not read on a page.
referee.publisher: BAR Smog Check Referee Program (asktheref.org); Department of Consumer Affairs blog (2021-08-04); BAR

law.summary: The SLEEP Act (Chapter 527 of the Laws of 2021; S784B) was signed on 2021-10-29 and took effect on 2022-04-01. It raised the maximum fine for illegal muffler and exhaust modifications to $1,000 ('an $850 increase'). Inspection stations must check that motorcycle mufflers and exhausts have not been illegally modified. A repair shop that willfully installs illegal equipment three times within 18 months risks losing its inspection station and operating certificates.
law.publisher: Office of the Governor of New York
law.effectiveDateNote: The date 2022-04-01 comes from secondary sources (NYCM Insurance blog and others); the governor's release doesn't give it.

sleepAct.statewideNote: No published count of statewide SLEEP Act (VTL §375(31)) tickets was found, from the State Police, the DMV/TSLED or any court system.

nycNoiseCameraEnforcement.caveat: This is New York City enforcement under the City Noise Code §24-236(e), under which DEP's camera summonses are issued (Local Law 7 of 2024). It is not SLEEP Act enforcement, but it is the only published count of loud-exhaust tickets found.

priorYears.conflict: Carscoops (2023-01-24) reported 71 camera tickets in 2022 with a minimum $800 penalty, against DEP's 102 for CY2022. DEP's figure is the primary source.

penaltyScale.detail: $800 for a first offense, up to $2,625 on a third-offense default (Carscoops; Brooklyn Eagle)
